newsitem.title: USA: Police make arrest in California bombing probe.
newsitem.headline: Police make arrest in California bombing probe.

text.p: Investigators said on Sunday they arrested one suspect and were searching for two others in connection with a series of bombings they believe were aimed at subverting the justice system.

Federal agents said they seized a vehicle containing about 60 sticks of explosives. The suspects were apparently planning to use the car bomb in an attack that could have been catastrophic, investigators said.
"We have developed solid evidence that should lead to a full conclusion of this case very shortly," Vallejo Police Chief Robert Nichelini told a crowded news conference at the Vallejo city hall.
"It is our belief that this was a deliberate attempt to stop the criminal justice system from operating in Solano County."
Two bombs exploded in Vallejo, 35 miles (50 km) northeast of San Francisco, in the last week, one outside a courthouse and one outside a bank. Both pre-dawn bombings caused damage but no injuries.
Last weekend, police also found and disarmed a bomb containing at least 30 sticks of dynamite that had been placed outside a public library that houses a police evidence room.
Nichelini said a task force of federal and local investigators arrested one man on Saturday night suspected of involvement in the bombings.

Police were searching for two other suspects whose whereabouts were unknown. Warrants have been issued for their arrest. Nichelini declined to identify any of the suspects and said it was possible more people were involved.

He said investigators had also served a number of search warrants and recovered a large quantity of explosives. Earlier on Sunday, police searched an apartment complex in Vallejo to gather evidence for the case.
Paul Snabel, the special agent in charge of the San Francisco office of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, said agents had found a vehicle containing about 60 sticks of explosives.

"The explosives were wired up and it was our understanding it was also to be used in a further attempt to subvert the justice system in Vallejo," Snabel said, adding the consequences of such a bomb exploding "could have been catastrophic."

Snabel said the bombers apparently intended to drive the vehicle to a target and detonate it. Investigators said they did not know what the planned target was. Snabel said the explosives found in the vehicle matched the explosives found at the library.

Nichelini said police were not sure if they had recovered all of the group's explosives and were still searching for other locations where their explosives might be stored. However, he said the possibility the group would carry out more bombings was "extremely remote."
Officials declined to give details of the group's alleged motive, but indicated they were planting the bombs because of a personal grudge rather than for political purposes.
Nichelini said police believed the bombings were "an attempt to stop pending hearings," but he would not say if the suspects were involved in any criminal cases.
He said the suspects were organized but were not "any sort of a militia group, or anything like that."
Nichelini said investigators believed the bank bombing may have been a diversion to throw the investigation off track and disguise the bombers' true motive.
Earlier this week, police released a photograph showing a shadowy figure taken by a surveillance camera at the bank that was bombed.
